issues.location: hooks/lib/planning-floor.sh:66-96,188-216; hooks/dev-cycle-check.sh:124-179 (and every G2 guard that calls sb_pf_write_records)
issues.problem: G2 ignores F2's unseen tier. When a command exceeds the analyser budget (~512 KiB), F2 returns status ok with writes:[], opaque:true, unseen_reasons:['command too large to analyze'] and no opaque_writers. Every G2 guard then sees no writes and allows the call silently, so the planning floor, state-tamper, contract, planning-file, instruction-file, trivial and workflow-chain guards are all bypassed by padding with a comment.
issues.evidence: python3 builds {tool_name:Bash, command:'<cmd>; # '+'a'*600000}, piped to each hook from the SB project, empty state. Commands: 'echo x > src/app.py', 'echo inst-a >> <SD>/state-test', 'echo x >> .planning/ROADMAP.md', 'echo hi > CLAUDE.md'. Result: dev-cycle-check, planning-file-guard, instruction-file-guard, trivial-file-guard and workflow-chain-guard all printed nothing (allow). Threshold: n=520000 -> HARD STOP, n=530000 -> none. sb_tool_input_load at 530000 gives status=ok, unseen_reasons=['command too large to analyze'].
issues.suggested_fix: In the shared loader path (planning-floor.sh), treat non-empty SB_SA unseen_reasons (or possible_actions containing 'unseen') as unanalysable. Core gates (dev-cycle-check PreToolUse, planning-file-guard, instruction/trivial guards in an SB project) deny with sb_pf_unanalysable_message, except for plain read-only commands, as G1 does with ca_unseen_reasons. Add a test per guard with a >budget payload.

issues.problem: A write whose destination is an ANCESTOR directory of the state dir (cp -r, cp -a, rsync -a, tar -x -C, unzip -d) is not treated as a write into it. Ancestry is checked only for rm/rmdir/unlink/'mv source'. One ordinary command can therefore replace the state file, arm the trivial marker or clear block records.
issues.evidence: mkdir -p $T/fake/.silver-bullet; : > $T/fake/.silver-bullet/trivial; dc_cmd "cp -r $T/fake/.silver-bullet $HOME/.claude/" -> none (trivial-file-guard -> none). After running it, ls <SD> shows 'trivial', and Edit src/app.js with empty state -> none (planning floor off). rsync -a /tmp/fake/ ~/.claude/ -> none. tar -xf s.tar -C $HOME -> none.
issues.suggested_fix: For every write record whose via is a directory-capable writer (cp -r/-a/-R, rsync, tar -x/-C, unzip -d, mv <dir>, git checkout/restore of a directory), treat the target as covering everything below it. Deny when a protected path (state dir, contract files, .planning protected set) is the target or lies under it. Prefer having F2 mark such writes 'recursive' so all guards share one rule.

issues.problem: R3-01 is closed only for shell-visible launches of a file named record-*.sh. Interpreter launches, find -exec and renamed copies still run the real recorder, forge planning state, and the forged state satisfies the planning floor.
issues.evidence: <cache>=$HOME/.claude/plugins/cache/alo-labs/silver-bullet/9.9.9 (copied hooks+templates), project all_tracked=[inst-a]. Each of these got verdict none from dev-cycle-check, and running it left state=[inst-a], after which Edit src/app.js was allowed: printf '<Skill payload>' | python3 -c 'import subprocess;subprocess.run(["bash","<cache>/hooks/record-skill.sh"])' ; ... | perl -e 'system("bash","<RS>")' ; ... | find <cache>/hooks -name 'record-sk*' -exec bash {} \; ; cp -r <cache>/hooks /tmp/hh && mv /tmp/hh/record-skill.sh /tmp/hh/x.sh && ... | bash /tmp/hh/x.sh.
issues.suggested_fix: (a) Extend the opaque_mentions rule to the recorder: deny an opaque writer or find -exec whose text names record-*.sh or the plugin hooks dir. (b) Treat an invoked script whose body matches a recorder (or that sources hooks/lib/hook-bootstrap.sh) as the recorder. (c) The real fix is G4's: record-skill must require the Skill tool channel or an adapter receipt. Mark R3-01 partial until G4 lands and track it.

issues.problem: Contract files can be renamed, replaced or deleted by interpreter one-liners. sb_pf_opaque_targets takes only words containing '/', and the contract basenames are not among the opaque_mentions needles (only .silver-bullet/ is). F2 catches open()/remove()/Path.write_text but not os.rename/os.replace/shutil.move or perl unlink.
issues.evidence: dc_cmd outputs, all 'none': python3 -c "import os;os.rename('silver-bullet.md','/tmp/x')" ; python3 -c "import os;os.replace('/tmp/x','.silver-bullet.json')" ; python3 -c "import shutil;shutil.move('silver-bullet.md','/tmp/x')" ; perl -e 'unlink "silver-bullet.md"'. os.replace with a prepared config (state.trivial_file=<SD>/branch or required_planning=[]) defeats R1-07/R2-04, because stop-check still honours trivial_file.
issues.suggested_fix: Add sb_pf_opaque_mentions silver-bullet.md .silver-bullet.json .silver-bullet.prompt.json (with silver-init/update recorded as the exception), and the .planning protected names for planning-file-guard. Add tests for os.rename/os.replace/shutil.move/perl unlink.

issues.problem: False positive: SB's own skills that legitimately write .silver-bullet.json through the agent are now hard-blocked. Only silver-init and silver-update unlock the file. skills/silver-add/SKILL.md:293-302 (GitHub project cache: jq ... .silver-bullet.json > $TMP && mv $TMP .silver-bullet.json) and skills/silver-devops/SKILL.md:57 (set project.active_workflow=devops-cycle) both fail.
issues.evidence: state inst-a silver-add silver-devops; dc_cmd 'TMP=$(mktemp)\njq ... .silver-bullet.json > "$TMP" && mv "$TMP" .silver-bullet.json' -> deny ENFORCEMENT CONTRACT PROTECTED. jq '.project.active_workflow="devops-cycle"' ... && mv /tmp/c .silver-bullet.json -> deny. Edit .silver-bullet.json full-dev-cycle->devops-cycle -> deny.
issues.suggested_fix: Either allow the specific skills (silver-add, silver-devops, any other config writer found by grep) the same way init/update are, or move those writes behind an SB-owned script that the guard recognises. Add honest-variant tests. Consider scoping the unlock to the most recently recorded skill rather than 'ever recorded on this branch', and note that the agent can invoke Skill silver-update just to unlock.

issues.problem: MCP file-write tools reach dev-cycle-check only. planning-file-guard and instruction-file-guard are not registered for mcp__*__write..., and dev-cycle-check does not protect .planning or CLAUDE.md, so an MCP filesystem server can write ROADMAP.md/STATE.md/milestone files or create CLAUDE.md freely. The G1 hand-off asked G2 for the MCP write matchers.
issues.evidence:
dev-cycle-check with {tool_name:'mcp__filesystem__write_file', tool_input:{path:'

/.planning/ROADMAP.md'}} -> none. The same for a new

/CLAUDE.md -> none. planning-file-guard denies that payload when invoked directly, but hooks.json never routes MCP tools to it.
issues.suggested_fix: Add the dev-cycle-check MCP write regex to the planning-file-guard and instruction-file-guard matcher groups. Filter by tool name inside the guard (as dev-cycle-check does) so read tools are not judged as writes: planning-file-guard currently denies a Read payload when handed one.

issues.problem: Required G1 hand-off not done: stop-check should call sb_trivial_path_trusted. It still honours a configured state.trivial_file pointing at any state-root file. Config protection mitigates this but is bypassable (issues 2 and 4).
issues.evidence: grep -rn sb_trivial_path_trusted hooks/ in G2 -> no matches. stop-check.sh:106 still reads .state.trivial_file.
issues.suggested_fix: Apply the hand-off (ignore a configured trivial_file in stop-check, or call G1's helper once both packages merge), or record an explicit cross-package dependency in the report.

issues.problem: Other state-tamper gaps of the same class: find <SD> -exec sh -c 'echo x >> {}' \; ; creating a symlink to the state dir and writing through it in the SAME command; python3 /tmp/w.py where the script file names the state path (invoked_script analysis covers shell scripts only).
issues.evidence: dc_cmd outputs, all none: find $SD -name state-test -exec sh -c 'echo inst-a >> {}' \; ; ln -s $SD /tmp/sdl; echo inst-a >> /tmp/sdl/state-test ; python3 $T/w.py (w.py appends to $HOME/.claude/.silver-bullet/state-test).
issues.suggested_fix: Treat ln -s whose source is (or contains) a protected dir as a protected write. Read an interpreter script argument (python/node/perl file) with the same opaque_mentions needles. Treat find -exec with a protected root as a write to it.

issues.problem: The 'cannot analyse' branch is meant to fail closed but fails open. cmd="$(printf ... | jq -r ...)" fails under pipefail for invalid JSON, and the ERR trap exits 0. A host normally cannot send such input, so the intent is simply dead.
issues.evidence: planning-file-guard with stdin '{"hook_event_name":"PreToolUse","tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"echo x >> .planning/ROADMAP.md' (truncated) -> no output (allow).
issues.suggested_fix: Append '|| true' to the jq extraction, as dev-cycle-check does, and add a test.

issues.problem: False positives and misleading messages. Read-only interpreter use of the state dir is denied as tamper ('runs inline code'), even for a script-file argument. Piping a plugin hook into bash is reported as a THIRD-PARTY PLUGIN BOUNDARY VIOLATION because the script body's relative writes resolve into the cache.
issues.evidence: node -e "console.log(require('fs').readFileSync(process.env.HOME+'/.claude/.silver-bullet/state','utf8'))" -> deny STATE TAMPER. python3 scripts/check.py ~/.claude/.silver-bullet/state -> deny 'inline code'. cat <cache>/hooks/record-skill.sh | bash -> deny 'THIRD-PARTY PLUGIN BOUNDARY VIOLATION via Bash command'.
issues.suggested_fix: Word the opaque deny accurately and suggest cat/jq for reading. Give recorder-by-stdin its own STATE TAMPER message.

issues.problem: Latency regression on file tools: every Edit/Write now starts python3 once in PreToolUse AND PostToolUse. Post only deletes the verify-tests marker but runs the full analysis first.

issues.suggested_fix: In PostToolUse for file tools, take file_path with jq and skip sb_tool_input_load (canonicalise in Bash). Short-circuit PostToolUse when no verify-tests marker exists.
